clue.text: Test a vehicle, reversing a tiny bit

indicators.note: reversing tells us the whole run test, a, vehicle is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles
a bus is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A tester puts a car through its paces by backing it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns all of MOT + A + BUS together, giving the letters in the opposite order. 'Test' looks like a verb but supplies MOT, the British vehicle inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle is smaller than an atom, so the word suits a very tiny piece of matter.

clue.text: Beat chums up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: chums are pals, close friends

explanation.surface: An order to give one's friends a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: To slap someone is to strike them, a synonym of beat in the hitting sense.

clue.text: Once tolerated idle chatter in shops abroad

parts.note: bode is an archaic past tense of bide, to put up with
gas is informal for empty talk

explanation.surface: Gossip that used to be put up with in foreign stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the old-fashioned form: BODE was a past tense of BIDE, as in 'bide one's time' or put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a small Spanish wine shop or grocery, so a shop found abroad.

clue.text: Character from overseas used to express a particular angle

definitions.meaning: a letter of a foreign alphabet, here the Greek one

definitions.text: used to express a particular angle
definitions.meaning: in geometry a Greek letter conventionally stands for an unknown angle

explanation.definitionFit: Theta is a Greek letter and the standard symbol mathematicians use to label an angle.

clue.text: One may have a particular sort of stroke to employ

definitions.text: One may have a particular sort of stroke to employ

parts.note: a masse is a billiards shot made with a near-vertical cue
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps a sportsman, has a special technique to put to work.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a massage therapist, whose strokes are her trade; read in pieces it is the billiards shot plus USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseuse is a woman who gives massages, working by stroking muscles.

clue.text: In favour of a word that may encapsulate wisdom

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a verb is a kind of word, a doing word

explanation.surface: Supporting a single word that might hold a grain of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short traditional saying that sums up accepted wisdom, like a saw or maxim.

clue.text: Sort of dwelling that's only half attractive and super

indicators.note: only half says just the first three of the six letters are kept

parts.note: pretty means attractive
fab, short for fabulous, means super or great

explanation.surface: A house described as only moderately appealing yet great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps PRE, the front half of PRETTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated house, a type of home built from factory-made sections.

clue.text: Awfully nasty bod hanging round end of town ready for action

indicators.note: hanging round says the jumbled letters surround another piece
awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of nasty bod are jumbled
end of picks the final letter of town

explanation.surface: An unpleasant character loiters about the edge of a town, poised to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' scrambles NASTYBOD into ONSTA..DBY, and 'hanging round' puts N, the last letter of town, in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on standby is to be waiting and ready to be called into action, an idiom.

clue.text: Longing to get rid of leader at work?

indicators.note: dropping the leader means the first letter of the longing word goes

parts.note: yearning is a longing, a strong desire

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a desire to topple the boss is felt at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like a workplace boss; it is the first letter, Y, of YEARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is earning is in paid employment, so the question mark admits a definition by example.

clue.text: Young American female, fighter ensnaring British boys surprisingly

indicators.note: ensnaring means holding something trapped inside

parts.note: a boxer is a fighter in the ring

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters of boys turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A girl in the States, a pugilist trapping some British lads to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' shuffles the boys; 'ensnaring' traps them, with B, inside the fighter. A bobby-soxer is an American teenage girl of the 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobby-soxer was an American teenage girl of the 1940s, named for her ankle socks.

clue.text: Named person seen quite close to the Queen's Head?

definitions.text: Named person seen quite close to the Queen's Head?

parts.words: Named person seen quite close to the Queen's Head?
parts.note: a British envelope carries a stamp bearing the monarch's head, and next to it is written the name of the person the letter is for; Queen's Head also looks like a pub name

explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the person named on an envelope, whose name sits near the stamp.

clue.text: Maybe an instruction not to slurp Polish drink

parts.words: Maybe an instruction not to slurp
parts.note: sh is the call for quiet that a noisy drinker might hear
to rub is to polish

explanation.surface: Perhaps telling someone to sip their Polish vodka quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised as a nationality but means polish, to RUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a drink made from fruit juice, sugar and spirit or vinegar.

clue.text: A tactile guy naughtily pinching a maiden going around capital

indicators.note: pinching means taking hold of, here enclosing a further piece
naughtily suggests misbehaviour, so the letters of a tactile guy run riot
going around turns the a and maiden pair to face the other way

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A touchy-feely man misbehaving by pinching a young woman, somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' scrambles the first three words; 'going around' turns 'a maiden' to read MA, which 'pinching' holds in the middle of the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala City is the capital of the Central American country of Guatemala.

clue.text: Iris, ill, refused to move

indicators.note: to move tells the letters of ill refused to shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A sick person called Iris would not budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman's name but is the flower, and the anagram of ILL REFUSED makes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleur-de-lis is a stylised lily or iris, and the name is also used for the iris plant itself.

clue.text: Lethargic and disorganised on a shopping trip?

definitions.meaning: a shopper with no written list of items is a muddle

explanation.definitionFit: Listless means lacking energy, and taken literally it means without a list.

clue.text: Look in, stopping son becoming gross

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or behold

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: in, as in staying in, means at home

explanation.surface: Dropping by blocks a boy from growing fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' looks like 'fat' in the surface, but means disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross in its sense of revolting or disgusting is a synonym of loathsome.

clue.text: Girl meeting soldier — love to be taken slowly

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
a GI is an American soldier
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman dates a serviceman and is told not to rush into romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is a musical direction meaning a passage is played at a slow pace.

clue.text: Shopkeeper is a fool, greeting monarch

parts.note: a clot is British slang for a fool
hi is a greeting
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A stallholder plays the idiot by saying hello to the King.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothier is a person who makes or sells clothes, so a kind of shopkeeper.

clue.text: Turmoil with loose woman entering Arab territory once

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: UAR was the United Arab Republic of Egypt and Syria, 1958 to 1971
pro is short for prostitute

explanation.surface: Chaos when a woman of loose morals turns up in the old Arab lands.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud public disturbance, a synonym of turmoil.

clue.text: Minister taken round a nuclear plant

indicators.note: taken round means the clergyman word goes around the a

parts.note: a rector is a minister of the church in charge of a parish

explanation.surface: A government minister is shown round a nuclear power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician; here it is a clergyman, RECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is the apparatus at the heart of a nuclear power station, so it stands for the plant.

clue.text: Sword to put down male, transfixing the heart

indicators.note: transfixing means piercing through, so one piece runs into the middle of the other

parts.note: the core is the heart of something
to lay is to put down

explanation.surface: A blade used to fell a man by running him through the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: LAY + M pierces CORE: C, then LAYM, then ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a large two-edged broadsword once used by Scottish Highlanders.

clue.text: Little old woman we bully

parts.note: O is the short form, a little version, of old
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A tiny elderly lady says 'we' are being pushed around.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe is to intimidate someone into submission, as a bully does.

clue.text: Spotted in bed, perhaps, quite inadequate

definitions.meaning: covered with the red rash of a childhood illness and confined to bed

explanation.definitionFit: Measly means having measles, with its spots, and also contemptibly small.

clue.text: Terrible punishment conveyed by what could be hated series of words

indicators.note: could be says the letters of hated might be rearranged into another word

parts.note: a sentence is a series of words

explanation.surface: A dreadful penalty expressed in words that might be loathed.
explanation.definitionFit: A death sentence is a court's order of execution, the most severe punishment.

clue.text: Emperor's drink

definitions.meaning: a title of the ruler of Ethiopia
a hot mix of wine, water, sugar and spice

explanation.definitionFit: Negus was the title of Ethiopian emperors and also a hot spiced wine drink.

clue.text: Ray can't finish game of cards

indicators.note: can't finish means the last letter of the fish word is lost

parts.note: a skate is a kind of ray, a flat fish

explanation.surface: A man named Ray is unable to complete a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name; it is the fish SKATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Skat is a three-player trick-taking card game popular in Germany.

clue.text: Fortune to come from this game?

definitions.text: Fortune to come from this game?

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a game might bring riches.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes a lottery game played for a fortune; in pieces it is LOT plus TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance with numbered draws in which a fortune may be won.

clue.text: Violently refuse to accept footwear

definitions.meaning: to fling something back forcefully, rejecting it
a shoe with a strap round the heel

explanation.definitionFit: A slingback is a woman's shoe held on by a strap behind the heel; to sling back is to hurl something back.

clue.text: Church that's distressed about occultism

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the distressed word goes around the church

parts.note: sorry means distressed or upset
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A parish that is upset about witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is the use of magic or occult powers, so it fits occultism.

clue.text: Most glowing stories may turn out to be false

indicators.text: may turn out to be false
indicators.note: turn out to be false suggests the letters of stories are not what they seem and get rearranged

explanation.surface: The most flattering tales may prove untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosiest means pinkest or most glowing, and also most optimistic.
